source: Built from the chapter's 2026-2027 Competitive Events Member Guide (PA FBLA). Check the official PA guideline and rubric before preparing.
intro: FBLA events are not all the same. Some are tests, some ask you to solve a case in a role play, and others involve building a project or giving a presentation. Pick something you are willing to practice consistently, not just something that sounds impressive.
choose: Start with what you like: business, finance, technology, design, speaking, or problem-solving.
Be honest about the format. Tests need steady studying; projects need planning and follow-through; role plays need both knowledge and speaking practice.
Check eligibility before committing, including grade restrictions, repeat-event rules, team size, and whether the event is offered at region or state.
For team events, choose people who communicate and follow through. Decide early who owns each task.
Read the rubric before making slides, writing a report, or building a project. It is the clearest checklist for what judges score.
routine: Week 1: Read the official guideline and rubric. Turn each requirement into a checklist.
Each week: Set one concrete goal, finish a practice set or project milestone, and review what went wrong.
Before competition: Do a timed run, test all files and links, and ask someone unfamiliar with your work to review it.
Keep a mistake log. Write what you missed, why, and what you will do differently next time.
official_rules: PA FBLA says the September 2026 Pennsylvania Competitive Events Guidelines are the official source if a website description conflicts with the PDF. Confirm event details, rubrics, deadlines, formats, grade limits, and entry limits in the current documents.

ai_intro: AI works best when you give it the real rubric and ask it to test you or review your work. It can get rules wrong, so check its answers against official materials. Follow event rules and adviser instructions about AI use.

ai_prompts.title: Turn the rubric into a checklist
ai_prompts.prompt: I am preparing for PA FBLA 2026–2027 [EVENT]. I will paste the official PA guideline and rubric. Turn every scored criterion and required rule into a plain-English checklist. Separate official requirements from optional advice. Do not invent requirements; flag anything unclear.

ai_prompts.title: Practice an objective test
ai_prompts.prompt: Using only the topic list I paste for [EVENT], ask me 15 challenging multiple-choice questions, one at a time. Wait for my answer, explain why it is right or wrong, and track my weak topics. Do not claim these are real competition questions.

ai_prompts.title: Practice a role play
ai_prompts.prompt: Act as a practice judge for [EVENT]. I will paste the official PA rules and topics. Give me one original case, wait for my response, then give specific feedback using the rubric I provide. Do not give the solution before I try.

ai_prompts.title: Review a presentation
ai_prompts.prompt: Here is the official rubric for [EVENT]. Ask me questions about my idea, audience, evidence, and plan. Review my outline against each criterion, identify missing pieces, and suggest improvements without writing the whole presentation for me.

ai_prompts.title: Audit a written project
ai_prompts.prompt: Using the official rubric and rules I paste for [EVENT], audit my outline section by section. Identify requirements I have not addressed, unsupported claims, and missing evidence. Do not invent sources or claim you checked something you have not seen.

ai_prompts.title: Practice a speech
ai_prompts.prompt: Give me an original practice prompt that fits the official rules I paste. Let me outline and respond first. Then review focus, organization, evidence, transitions, and delivery, and give me one drill for my weakest area.

ai_prompts.title: Prepare for software testing
ai_prompts.prompt: Based on the official reference guide I provide for [EVENT], create a practice task that tests similar skills without copying a real test. Give me the task first, then a self-check list.

ai_prompts.title: Plan a team project
ai_prompts.prompt: Help our team plan [EVENT]. Ask us to assign roles, deadlines, and deliverables. Compare our plan to the official rubric I provide and flag missing responsibilities, duplicated work, and risks.

ai_prompts.title: Final rubric review
ai_prompts.prompt: Here is my work and the official PA rubric. Review each criterion separately. Explain what my work demonstrates, identify the gap, and suggest the next revision. Be specific and do not invent a score.

checklist: I read the current PA guideline and rubric for my exact event.
I checked eligibility, team size, repeat-event restrictions, and conference level.
I know the deadline, file type, time limit, and submission method.
I have practiced under realistic conditions at least once.
I checked all files, links, visuals, and backups.
I can explain my decisions without reading every word off a slide.
I checked AI-generated claims against official materials and followed the event's AI rules.
checklist_closing: Prepare early, use the rubric, and keep getting better with every practice run.
